checkpoints: A burst of multiple edits saves exactly once, 120 ms after the latest edit, with the latest accepted text.
A new edit after a completed save starts a fresh 120 ms burst and saves successfully.
An empty-string edit is saved rather than treated as absent pending work.
Editing with no current Badge remains a no-op.
Switching documents, reopening the same document, closing, and disposing with a pending edit preserve that edit for its original document and clean up the departing subscription.

If a synchronous store listener navigates during a timer-driven or retirement-driven save, the nested navigation remains authoritative and the superseded open does not install or render its destination.
Caller mutation after edit acceptance cannot alter the text eventually saved.
Preview retains its existing 40 ms trailing behavior and hide cancellation.
forbidden_effects: Do not write every accepted edit directly to the store.
Do not associate pending text with whichever document happens to be current when the timer fires.
Do not cancel or discard an accepted document edit merely because its Badge is detached.
Do not destroy a store-owned document buffer when a view retires.
Do not let an outer open overwrite or render over navigation performed synchronously by a save listener.
Do not emit status for a document other than the current Badge's document.
Do not change Preview timing, cancellation, payloads, or public interfaces.
Do not alter source identity, text, revision, or status payload semantics.
lifecycle_identity: Each accepted edit belongs to the Badge and document buffer that were current when edit was called.
BufferBank is store-owned, and its Trailing entry is persistent and reusable per document ID across Badge lifetimes.
Badge owns only its live store subscription; detaching the Badge must not destroy its document buffer.
Each open request is identified by the workspace generation captured before retirement; a request superseded by synchronous navigation must not install a Badge or render a document.
Accepted text must be copied at acceptance so delayed saving retains the same value semantics as the original synchronous Store#write path.

obligations.text: Workspace#edit must remain a no-op without a current Badge; otherwise it must capture the current Badge's buffer and enqueue an acceptance-time copy of the supplied text instead of writing immediately.
Each document buffer must use the existing Trailing utility with a 120 ms delay, resetting the timer for each edit in the burst and writing only the latest accepted text after the quiet interval.
After a burst is consumed, the same per-document buffer must accept and save later independent bursts, including an empty-string edit.

Before invoking Store#write, Trailing#flush must retire the consumed handle and pending value so synchronous reentry cannot consume the same value twice and an edit accepted during the callback can form a subsequent burst.

When a Badge retires, Workspace must revoke it as current, detach its captured subscription, clear the document presentation, and flush its pending document buffer so switch, reopen, close, and dispose preserve the original editor's persistence behavior.

Because retirement flushing may synchronously invoke navigation through store listeners, Workspace#open must revalidate its captured generation after retirement and must not install or render a superseded destination.
Store behavior must remain synchronous and retain copied record text, monotonically increasing revisions, listener notification behavior, and original event field semantics.
The public Workspace and Preview interfaces must remain unchanged, and Preview must remain outside this change.

ordering_barriers: On edit acceptance: capture the current Badge and its document buffer, copy the text, then push that copy into the captured buffer.
On trailing consumption: cancel the active handle, snapshot the pending value, clear both handle and pending state, then call the store-writing work callback.
On retirement: capture the departing Badge, clear @current, detach its subscription, publish the cleared document, then flush its captured buffer.

On open: increment and capture @generation before retirement; after retirement and any callback-capable flush, compare the captured request with the current generation before obtaining/installing the destination Badge or rendering its document.
Store#write must update the copied record and revision before synchronously notifying subscribed listeners.
preservation: Preserve Workspace methods open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose(), and Preview methods query(text) and hide().
Preserve independent per-document BufferBank entries and their reuse across visits.
Preserve document clearing and rendering behavior apart from the required delayed write timing.
Preserve current-document-only status filtering and subscription removal.
Preserve Store read/write copying, revision increments, event fields, and synchronous notification semantics.
Preserve the original document association of accepted text across navigation.
Preserve Preview's separate 40 ms quiet interval and hide cancellation.
scope: Business code governing Workspace draft edits, Trailing task consumption, per-document BufferBank ownership, Badge retirement, and navigation safety in src/workflow.rb.
Only document autosave timing changes: active editing moves from a write per keystroke to one latest-value write after 120 ms of quiet.
Search Preview is explicitly out of scope except that its existing behavior must remain intact.

def initialize(env);@task=Trailing.new(env,40){|q| env.output('preview',{'query'=>q})};end
 def query(text);@task.push(text);end
 def hide;@task.cancel;end

triggers: Workspace#edit(text) while a Badge is current.
A second or later edit before the current 120 ms timer fires.
Expiration of 120 ms without another edit for that document buffer.
Workspace#open(id), Workspace#close, or Workspace#dispose while the departing buffer has pending text.
A synchronous store listener calling navigation during a timer-driven or retirement-driven save.
Preview#query(text) and Preview#hide only as preservation checks.
unknowns: The public sources specify no exception-handling policy for Store listeners, output sinks, timer scheduling, cancellation, or cleanup.

The task does not state a universal persistence deadline for all persistent buffers; flushing on this editor's retirement is derived from preserving its prior synchronous persistence across open, close, and dispose.
Reentry from document or status output sinks is not documented; synchronous navigation is established specifically for store listeners.
Timer ordering for callbacks scheduled at the same instant is unspecified.
No requirement is established to cancel already-started persistent saves during dispose.
